findings: 2026-11-06: drafted for Mathematics 12 Unit 1 (owner request): English and a teacher-style Roman Urdu lesson; the book's content in order with our clearly labelled teaching notes; worked examples step by step with reasons; results verified with sympy.

Book correction: The book prints "Formally the vertical line y = c is called horizontal asymptote". A line y = c is horizontal, not vertical. Correct: the horizontal line y = c is called a horizontal asymptote of y = f(x) if f(x) \to c as x \to -\infty or x \to \infty.

Book correction: Four entries in the book's tables are cut off (truncated) instead of rounded: e^{3} = 20.0855\ldots \approx 20.086 (printed 20.085); e^{10} = 22026.4658\ldots \approx 22026.466 (printed 22026.465); e^{-1} = 0.36788\ldots \approx 0.368 (printed 0.367); e^{-3} = 0.049787\ldots \approx 0.0498 (printed 0.0497). The book's own Figure 1.6 uses the rounded value (-1, 0.37).

Book correction: The book prints \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{-100} = 1.267 \times 10^{30}. In fact 2^{100} = 1.26765\ldots \times 10^{30}, which rounds to 1.268 \times 10^{30} (the printed value is cut off, not rounded).
